hook.text: Pork is forbidden in Islam and Judaism. Beef is sacred in Hinduism. Each rule tells a story.

buildup.text: Food taboos usually start practical—pork spoiled fast in desert heat—and become sacred law.

discovery.text: Anthropologist Marvin Harris argued every food taboo had an economic or ecological root.

twist.text: India's cow protection wasn't always religious. Cattle were too valuable as draft animals to eat.

climax.text: Food bans mark group identity. What you won't eat says who you belong to.

punchline.text: Your menu is a membership card.

quiz.question: Who argued that food taboos have economic or ecological origins?
